tagline: Stone-walled hilltop farms, at a speed limit the state kept.
intro: Route 49 leaves Route 184 in North Stonington as Pendleton Hill Road and heads north into Voluntown. Past the town center it becomes Ekonk Hill Road, crosses the Pachaug River and runs through Pachaug State Forest, the largest in the state's system, before it ends on Sterling Hill and Route 14A carries on east.

The prize is the view from big hilltop farms fenced with stone walls, cattle grazing and corn growing tall. A 2003 plan for the corridor named its concerns as speed, stone walls and the scenery. North Stonington asked that year to bring the 45 mph limit down. The state said no.

moments.title: Voluntown
moments.text: The town takes its name from the colonial volunteers of King Philip's War, men who stayed to fight "and went not away".

moments.title: Pachaug State Forest
moments.text: More than 27,000 acres along the Pachaug River, with an Atlantic white cedar swamp at Great Meadow and a boardwalk trail through a rhododendron sanctuary.

moments.title: Sterling
moments.text: Rochambeau's army marched through and camped here in 1781, coming from Narragansett Bay to join Washington on the Hudson.
